Coverage gap this FEAT must close: nothing today references `shouldPreserveCursorForReason`, so the fail-safe `?? true` default in crew/scripts/lib/cost-hygiene/cost-report-guard.mts could be flipped to `?? false` and every suite in both test trees would stay green. mock.module fragility: src/tests/cost-scan-cursor-honesty-guard.test.mts documents empirically that registering mock.module a second time for the same path loses the first registration, so new reason cases must extend the existing mutable `handlerMode` switch rather than adding a second mock. A builder who adds a parallel registration will get confusing, order-dependent failures.

scopeNotes: SCOPE CORRECTION -- the live tree is materially different from the FEAT body in four ways, all verified by grep on 2026-11-06. (a) The rewrite surface is LARGER than stated. The FEAT says 91 refs in commands and 42 in agents (133 total); actual occurrence counts are `crew/scripts/crew.mts` 93 in commands/ + 44 in agents/ (excluding agents/3rdparty/) + 8 in skills/, and `src/scripts/loop.mts` 42 in commands/ + 9 in agents/ + 8 in skills/, plus prune-artifacts.mts 2 in commands/ and watch-tick.mts 1 in commands/ -- about 207 occurrences across roughly 57 files (31 commands, 19 agents, 7 skills). The FEAT also omits skills/ from its stated counts while naming it in the deliverable. (b) THREE deliverable bullets are no-ops as written and should be dropped rather than attempted: `crew/scripts/report-to-pr.mts` has zero occurrences anywhere in commands/, agents/, skills/ or templates/; templates/ has zero occurrences of any of the five scripts; and CLAUDE.md has zero occurrences, so there is no marker-block rewrite to do -- which is just as well, since AGENTS.md Never-do forbids hand-editing those blocks. (c) The validator rule is genuinely new work: grep finds no `no-source-script-path` rule in crew/scripts/validate-agents.mts and no commands/*.md sibling check today. (d) dist/ is present and complete as FEAT-026 shipped it: dist/crew.js, dist/loop.js, dist/prune-artifacts.js, dist/report-to-pr.js, dist/watch-tick.js and 11 dist/hooks/*.js bundles, with `bun run build:dist` wired to src/scripts/build-dist.mts. SEQUENCING: the FEAT body's "serial on the shared branch, not a wave lane" is a real constraint and must be honored -- the six proposed slices touch overlapping product-surface globs and the ratchet drain depends on all three rewrite slices landing first, so they are sequential, not a parallel wave. Smallest deliverable: slices 1 and 2 (commands + agents) alone clear all 42 EXPECTED_FAIL entries, because listShippedEntrypoints sources CLI entries only from those two markdown globs; skills/, the validator rule and the docs updates are hardening that stops the regression from recurring. Grade weak dimensions (Framework 4, last-5 averages from .claude/artifacts/loop/loop-snapshot.md): NONE below 0.80 -- lowest is security 0.862, then observability 0.894 -- so no weak-dimension AC is owed, though AC-2 doubles as the observability guard on the gate itself. Effort calibration (Framework 5): nearest analogs are SLICE-52 (FEAT-026, the dist bundling this directly follows) at $30.77 and SLICE-46 (FEAT-033) at $26.39 / 14 min. This work is mechanically simpler than SLICE-52 -- no resolver archaeology -- but reaches far more files, and consumer-smoke stages a ~269 MB tree per call under a 180 s default timeout, so each verification cycle is slow and the suite cannot be iterated cheaply. That pushes effort to 0.6 (8 points) rather than 0.5, which trips the decomposition gate; proposedSlices below carries six entries summing to 10 points at the 2-point cap.
risks: Pre-mortem 1 -- most likely cause of a failed review or validation two weeks out: a blanket find-and-replace. Three distinct traps. It must not rewrite agents/3rdparty/ (vendored and exempt per AGENTS.md), it must not rewrite prose and docs examples that describe development rather than shipped invocation (CLAUDE.md and docs/ deliberately stay on source paths), and -- the subtle one -- src/scripts/lib/install/shipped-entrypoints.mts sources CLI entries ONLY from literal invocations in commands/*.md and agents/*.md, so a rewrite that changes the literal shape in a way the extractor no longer recognizes would shrink the entry list and turn gate 42 green by discovering nothing instead of by passing. AC-2 exists specifically to make that failure mode impossible to merge.

Pre-mortem 2 -- merged and broke the loop, what rollback requires: `git revert` of a markdown-plus-test-file commit is sufficient. No migration, no state cleanup, no cross-plugin coordination. The only contract-shaped change is gate 42 flipping from designed-red to blocking, and the same revert restores it. dist/ itself is untouched by this FEAT, so FEAT-026's bundles are not at risk.

Pre-mortem 3 -- which existing test would NOT catch a regression here: nothing today asserts that a product-surface file may not name a source script path. That is precisely the `no-source-script-path` rule this FEAT adds. Until it exists, a later edit can reintroduce `bun crew/scripts/crew.mts ...` into a command and the only thing that would notice is a full consumer-smoke run (gate 42, ~180 s plus a 269 MB staging copy) -- too slow and too coarse to protect the invariant, which is why the validator rule is not optional polish.

Entry-list honesty gap, documented by the suite itself at src/tests/install/consumer-smoke.test.mts:15-23: `crew/scripts/crew.mts show-workflow-state` is not invoked via bun anywhere in commands/*.md or agents/*.md today (commands/build.md reads workflow-state.json via jq instead; FEAT-029 would switch it), so it is absent from the entry list and cannot appear in EXPECTED_FAIL. Draining the set to empty therefore does NOT prove every real invocation runs -- it proves every DISCOVERED one does. Do not let the green gate be reported as stronger than it is, and expect FEAT-029 to add entries later.

Blast radius is wide even though each edit is trivial: roughly 57 files across four product surfaces that ship to adopter repos. AGENTS.md Never-do warns against casually editing commands/, agents/, skills/ and templates/ -- here that editing IS the deliverable, but it means a careless slice can degrade the shipped product surface broadly in one commit. Per-surface slices (1, 2, 3) keep each diff reviewable.

Merge-order hazard carried from SLICE-52's grade lesson: "The dist freshness gate is a merge gate as much as a commit gate: after merging two sibling lanes that changed bundled sources, build:dist --check went red for 10 bundles." This FEAT does not change bundled sources, so it should not trip that gate -- but it runs serially on a shared branch alongside other audit work, so `bun src/scripts/build-dist.mts --check` belongs in the AC-7 gate list to catch a sibling lane's drift rather than this FEAT's.

Second-order: gate 42 becoming blocking makes a slow, 269 MB-staging suite a hard merge gate for everyone on the branch. If it proves flaky on the self-hosted runner, the pressure will be to re-add EXPECTED_FAIL entries rather than fix the cause -- the exact anti-pattern the ratchet comment at lines 9-13 forbids. docs/ci-gates.md should record the retry policy alongside the blocking flip.
